trigger.authentication_note: Google Drive dennis@work.flowers. The SAME connection is needed twice: here on the trigger (which polls the folder) and as the `gdrive` alias in --connections, because the workflow code renames the file.
trigger.trigger_note: Polling trigger (New File in Folder) on the Signed Agreements folder. No webhook_url — nothing external needs a catch URL. The classic Zap 'Legal Agreement Summarizer' also polls this same folder; every one of its downstream steps was paused:true in the export (normal for a classic Zap export, not evidence of its live/run status either way), so there is no duplicate-processing risk from leaving it as-is.

connectionless_apps.AICLIAPI: get_completion — authentication_id "0" (Included in Plan), no connection

notion.template_note: create_database_item with template_mode:"default" threw 'no default template is configured for this data source' on the live run below; createItemWithTemplate's fallback create path was taken. Per repo rule 5 the template path is still attempted first, so no code change is needed if a default template is added later.
notion.properties_note: The AI step extracts Counterparty and Contract Signed Date (needed for the file rename and the page title) but neither is written as a Notion property — a separate Notion-side agent, triggered on new pages in this data source, reads the attached PDF and populates everything else, including Agreement Type. Agreement Type classification was tried during development (first a 4-option set, then a consolidated 9-category taxonomy) but was dropped entirely — it fed only the file/page name, never a Notion property, so Dennis asked to remove the AI call's classification burden rather than keep an unused output field.

ai_model.tier_note: standard/auto verified sufficient across 7 real documents pulled from the live Signed Agreements folder via the offline run-action harness — see the README's verified-cases table (that testing pre-dates dropping Agreement Type, but the Counterparty fix it validated is unchanged). No tier upgrade needed; the fix was prompt/schema quality (an explicit exclusion list for the company's own entity as counterparty, an explicit empty-string rule for internal-only documents).

live_runs.note: One production run to date, through the deployed durable (not a synthetic payload), against a real previously-unfiled document. Predates the current version (which dropped Agreement Type) but exercised the same rename + Notion-create + file-attach mechanism unchanged.

runs.file: Terms and Conditions for pre-paid Talk Therapy Sessions.pdf (previously unfiled since 2025-03-20)
runs.outcome: Renamed and filed into Notion (Agreement Name + File Link only; PDF attached; usedTemplate false). Also returned an Agreement Type value at the time, which was never written to Notion and has since been removed from the workflow entirely.

replaces_classic_zap.title: Legal Agreement Summarizer
replaces_classic_zap.old_shape: Drive trigger (New File in Folder, Signed Agreements) -> AI extraction of 9 fields (currency, amount, counterparty, effective date, end date, agreement type, signatory emails, signed date, free-text summary) -> rename file -> Formatter email extraction -> branch on signatory email resolved via Zapier Table -> create_database_item (with or without Signatory relation) -> upload_file_to_page_block
replaces_classic_zap.status: Classic Zap left as-is (safe — its trigger polls the same folder but every downstream step is paused, so no duplicate-processing risk). Turning its trigger off too is optional, not required.
